title: Due dates for tasks
body:
Tasks need deadlines. Add an optional due date:

- The new-task form gets a date field; a task with no date stays valid and unchanged.
- Cards with a due date show it in plain language (for example `Due Oct 24`).
- A task whose due date has passed and that is not done is marked as overdue — clear at a glance, not alarming.
- Tasks already stored in someone's browser have no due date; they must keep working.

Put the date logic in `src/lib/tasks.ts` as small pure helpers (set, clear, overdue check, label) with unit tests, and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. This is a visible UI change, so leave the visual proof in the artifacts folder.

title: Order the columns: priority, then due date
body:
Within each column, order tasks by what matters: priority first (high, then normal, then low), then the nearest due date, then oldest first. Tasks without a due date sort after dated ones within the same priority.

The order must be deterministic and derivable from the task fields alone. Put the ordering in `src/lib/tasks.ts` as a pure comparator with unit tests, and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. This changes how the board reads, so leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder.

title: Filter bar: status, priority and overdue
body:
The board now holds enough tasks that finding things matters. Add a filter bar above the columns:

- A status filter: All / To do / Doing / Done.
- A priority filter: All / High / Normal / Low.
- An `Overdue only` toggle for tasks past their due date and not done.
- Column counts reflect what is shown; an empty result says so; one click clears every filter.

Filters are display-only: they must never change or hide stored tasks. Put the filtering in `src/lib/tasks.ts` as a pure function with unit tests, and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. Visible UI change: leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder.

title: Header callout for overdue work
body:
When something is overdue, the header should say so without being asked: extend the progress summary with a distinct callout like `2 overdue` whenever the count is above zero, styled to catch the eye with the existing palette. At zero, nothing appears.

The count comes from the same task list the columns render. Keep the logic in `src/lib/tasks.ts` with a unit test (including the zero case), and keep the three commands in `AGENTS.md` passing. Visible UI change: leave before/after proof in the artifacts folder.
